Systems.RateScale: Controls tread consumption. Higher values use tyres faster; zero restores the original disabled consumption setting for this supported build. Native worn-tyre grip is retained. No fixed tyre lifetime is promised.
Systems.WetTarmac: Reduces the wet-tarmac loss coefficient. More reduction makes this part of wet-road grip loss gentler, not that percentage more grip. Dry-road grip and tyre slip curves are unchanged.
Systems.VisualDamage: Scales body-deformation input. A higher value can make dents more visible; it does not multiply crash forces or mechanical health loss. Stock preserves ordinary body damage.
Systems.CollisionDamage: Scales health loss from eligible contacts. Higher values are more punishing; they do not increase impact forces. Recommended uses a separate 1.50x override, shown beneath the preset.
Systems.TyreDamage: Enables native compression-related tyre damage. This is a processing switch, not a puncture chance or a guarantee that every hit punctures a tyre. Other native conditions remain in control.
Systems.MechanicalFailures: Determines how early a damaged component becomes eligible for the native failure checks. Higher health thresholds permit checks after less damage. An 85% threshold is NOT an 85% failure chance.
Systems.BrakeWear: Enables the native disc and pad consumption routine. Native temperatures, braking forces and material limits determine the amount. No duplicate brake-fade penalty is added.
Systems.Detachment: Scales break thresholds for authored breakable attachments. Smaller factors allow earlier separation; unbreakable parts remain unbreakable. This is not restricted to cosmetic panels.
Systems.CriticalDamage: Allows eligible collision and mechanical failures to reach the native Critical state. It does not add fixed health loss or a random failure chance. Severe damage can end a run.
Systems.CoolingRouting: Adds approximate engine-bay impact coverage when a cooling socket is missing. Dedicated sockets take precedence. Optional modeled heat is a different control under Engine and turbo response; it is not a native coolant-leak simulation.
Systems.EngineImpact: Weights collision damage reaching the Engine part. Higher values make engine hits more consequential; they do not directly multiply horsepower loss. It interacts with collision scaling and native health limits.
Systems.PowerResponse: Makes existing engine/turbo damage affect performance before complete failure. Caps never increase the original response. Tune numbers contains separate optional cooling and routine engine-wear controls; each is described independently.
Systems.WheelImpact: Distributes impact effects by distance to eligible wheel hubs. Bending and optional toe/camber changes use actual wheel damage, without inventing controller steering. Unequal damage can cause pull; symmetric damage need not pull to one side.
Systems.GearboxDamage: Enables grinding, engine-hit transfer and progressively reluctant shifting. Recommended preserves healthy shifts and the softened internal-life response. Severe component damage can still prevent shifts. Stress measures actual coupled over-rev exposure, not a fixed penalty per paddle press.

Controls.WearScale: Higher means faster tread consumption. Overrides the selected coefficient, not a fixed lifetime or an extra grip penalty.
Controls.WetLossScale: Smaller means less wet-tarmac loss from this coefficient. 1.00 retains stock; this is not a measured grip multiplier.
Controls.VisualScale: Higher amplifies deformation input. Native limits remain; it does not directly scale mechanical damage.
Controls.CollisionScale: Higher scales eligible collision health loss. Recommended is 1.50x. Contact geometry and clamping still matter.
Controls.EngineImpactFactor: Higher increases Engine-only collision weighting. Recommended keeps 4.00x. Does not alter routine wear.
Controls.EngineResponseThreshold: Remaining-health fraction below which the extra engine cap acts. Higher begins performance loss earlier; it does not change health.
Controls.TurboResponseThreshold: Remaining-health fraction below which the extra turbo cap acts. Higher starts the cap earlier; not measured boost.
Controls.GearboxImpactFraction: Share of actual engine collision health-fraction loss transferred to the gearbox. 0.50 means half. Wear and repairs do not transfer.
Controls.GearboxGrindingRate: Higher increases native grinding-wear input. Clean shifts are not charged a fixed penalty.
Controls.GearboxEngagementGain: Higher adds delay to damaged ordinary shifts. Healthy shifts retain native timing.
Controls.GearboxRecovery: Minimum pause after a rejected damaged shift, in seconds. Higher makes rapid retries less effective; longer native waits remain.
Controls.GearboxStressExposure: Higher increases gearbox stress from actual coupled downshift over-rev. Recommended keeps 0.12. No penalty merely for requesting a downshift.
Controls.SuspensionGain: Higher amplifies only native damage-related steering-joint displacement. It does not move the steering input.
Controls.SuspensionLimit: Upper size of the added bending amplification, in native length units. Existing larger native damage is not reduced.
Controls.GearboxProgression: Lets internal gearbox life contribute to shift difficulty using the softened response. Healthy timing stays normal; component damage remains separate.
Controls.DifferentialWearRate: Fallback only when the authored differential wear rate is zero. Higher increases eligible material use. Existing nonzero rates and material limits remain.
Controls.SuspensionAlignmentDegrees: Maximum added toe angle, scaled by each wheel damage level. Higher can increase damaged-car scrub or instability; it is not a fixed steering pull.
Controls.SuspensionCamberDegrees: Maximum added camber angle, scaled per wheel and mirrored by side. Higher strengthens geometry consequences without steering-input injection.
Controls.CoolingConsequences: Enables the added damage-sensitive cooling/heat model. Temperature is modeled, not native coolant telemetry. No fluid-leak simulation is claimed.
Controls.CoolingHealthThreshold: Health fraction used by the cooling-efficiency cap. Higher can reduce cooling efficiency earlier after damage; it does not change impact health loss.
Controls.CoolingStressRate: Higher scales added engine-wear exposure when the model overheats. Zero removes this added heat penalty, not native over-rev or collision damage.
Controls.HudDamageWarnings: Makes dashboard warnings reflect operational engine/gearbox degradation. Critical can mean currently unusable, not necessarily permanently destroyed. No extra damage is added.
Controls.EngineUseWearScale: Multiplies only routine Engine-use wear. Recommended is 0.50x. Zero does not prevent collision, over-rev, boost, thermal damage or other failure paths.
